pages.title: Health and safety program at Utilitek Solutions Inc.

domains.name: Compliance Documentation
domains.path: Quality Management/Quality Control/Safety & Regulatory Compliance/Compliance Documentation

sections.body: According to Utilitek Solutions Inc., protecting workers from injury or occupational disease is a major continuing objective. The company states that, as employer, it is ultimately responsible for worker health and safety. Supervisors at Utilitek Solutions Inc. are held accountable for the health and safety of workers under their supervision. Every worker is also responsible and accountable for their individual health and safety performance. The most recent review of the Health & Safety Program took place on April 16, 2025.
sections.title: Responsibilities and policy statement

sections.body: Utilitek Solutions Inc. adopts the emergency response plan of the owner or operator when working at client locations. For its office, the fire evacuation gathering point is the northwest corner of 176 St and 106 Ave. Workplace harassment and violence are prohibited on the company's work sites. Employees receive yearly training on workplace violence and harassment. Reported harassment or violence incidents are investigated, with review commencing within 24 hours of report review and investigations completed within 90 days. Investigation reports are retained for at least two years. Reviews of the workplace violence and harassment prevention program take place at least annually. Records of all program reviews are kept for a minimum of three years.
sections.title: Emergency response and violence and harassment prevention

sections.body: Under Utilitek Solutions Inc.'s Discipline Policy, which defines unacceptable behavior on its jobsites and corrective measures, Class A violations (fighting, theft or willful destruction of property, drug and alcohol policy violations, and willful endangerment) warrant immediate termination. Class B violations, such as dishonesty, harassment, insubordination, unsafe behavior, and safety rule violations, require disciplinary action that may include termination. Utilitek Solutions Inc. categorizes PPE as basic, meaning hard hats, safety glasses, safety footwear, and appropriate clothing worn at all times by all personnel, and specialized, meaning gloves, welder's goggles, respiratory protection, fall arrest equipment, and special clothing for specific jobs or hazards. Employee-owned PPE is not allowed. All employees are required to immediately report accidents, incidents causing injury or property damage, and near misses to their supervisor. Supervisors report promptly to management for timely submission to the applicable worker's compensation board, and critical injuries are reported to the authorities by senior management. Injured employees are provided with a modified work program until they can return to their pre-accident job wherever possible. Before modified duty starts, the employee and employer sign an agreement covering hours of work, reporting requirements, and the nature of the position. The employee supplies medical progress reports every two weeks or as frequently as needed. Utilitek Solutions Inc. states that protection of workers from injury or occupational disease is a major continuing objective and that the company, as employer, is ultimately responsible for worker health and safety. Utilitek Solutions Inc. holds regular safety meetings every week. A daily tailgate meeting is documented at the beginning of each workday when two or more employees, subcontractor representatives, or client representatives are present at a job site, and late arrivals are briefed on the topics and sign the form. Utilitek Solutions Inc.'s Health & Safety Program was last reviewed on April 16, 2025. Supervisors are held accountable for the health and safety of workers under their supervision, and every worker is responsible and accountable for their individual health and safety performance. Utilitek Solutions Inc. employees receive WHMIS training at orientation, as a refresher at least once every three years, or upon program change, and training records are maintained. A designated Safety Representative ensures an SDS is available for all regulated chemicals, reviews SDSs for updates at least once every three years, and participates in planned workplace inspections. Employees must advise management of deteriorated labels or missing SDSs, and an up-to-date SDS log book is maintained at the shop in a clearly visible location. Hearing protection is required for employees exposed to noise of 85 dB or greater, generally whenever voices must be elevated to be heard. The company will also develop a Hearing Conservation Program for workers consistently exposed to noise over 85 dB. When working at client locations, Utilitek Solutions Inc. adopts the emergency response plan of the owner/operator; for its office, the fire evacuation gathering point is the northwest corner of 176 St and 106 Ave. All employees participate in an annual health and safety orientation, conducted by a supervisor or competent designate, along with a site-specific orientation when reporting to a new site. These orientations cover site safety standards, first aid locations, and posted legislation, and all orientation records are documented and filed in the employee file. Planned, documented workplace inspections at Utilitek Solutions Inc. identify and correct unsafe conditions and behavior. They cover premises, job sites, buildings, temporary structures, excavations, tools, equipment, machinery, and work practices. Inspections occur weekly on project sites and monthly at the company premises, with supervisors and the health and safety representative involved. The company prohibits workplace harassment and violence on its work sites and trains employees on workplace violence and harassment yearly. Reported harassment or violence incidents are investigated, with review commencing within 24 hours of report review and investigations completed within 90 days. Investigation reports are retained for at least two years, and the prevention program is reviewed at least annually with review records kept for a minimum of three years.
